summary: Drive-up L-4 lookout on Sugarloaf Peak (Wenatchee NF, WA), staffed every summer since 1914; its cab was moved from Lion Rock in 1949 and fires threatened it in 1970, 1994 and 2025.

facts.design: L-4 cab built at Lion Rock (1932 per Willhite and firelookout.com; 1933 per NHLR), moved to Sugarloaf in 1949 to replace a D-6 cupola cabin

staffing.status: staffed every summer (NHLR, firelookout.com and Willhite; the pages are undated)

access.note: Drive-up on gravel roads; a gate on the spur road means a short walk to the lookout (about a quarter mile per WTA). Staffed lookout where visitors are welcomed.

visit.trail_note: Gravel route via Eagle Creek Road off Highway 209 and Van Creek Road (NF 7520); about 6 miles to the ridge road junction, then the spur road to the gate and a short walk (WTA, Willhite).

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Wenatchee National Forest (Entiat Ranger District cooperator)

events.note: First used for fire detection with a heliograph station on the summit; the first station was just a camp
D-6 cupola cabin added on the summit (WTA dates the start of lookout activity to 1924)
L-4 cab built at Lion Rock (Willhite and firelookout.com); NHLR describes a 1933-vintage cab
L-4 cab moved from Lion Rock to the summit in sections, replacing the cupola cabin
Entiat Fire (120,000 acres) threatened the lookout
Tyee-Hatchery Fire threatened the lookout; the cab was saved by a Fort Lewis fire crew, but the outhouse burned (NHLR also says the garage burned)
Lower Sugarloaf fire threatened the lookout (firelookout.com)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Willhite and firelookout.com say the L-4 cab was built at Lion Rock in 1932; NHLR describes a 1933-vintage cab. The story reports both; the event is kept at 1932 with the NHLR figure noted.
NHLR and Willhite place the first fire-detection station on the summit in 1914; WTA says lookout activity started in 1924. The story reports both.
NHLR says the outhouse and garage burned; Willhite and firelookout.com mention only the outhouse. Both are reported in the story.
NHLR gives 5,729 ft (1,746 m), matching the record's 1746.2 m; firelookout.com gives 5814 ft. No change proposed.

notes_for_editor: Record matches NHLR on elevation, registration date (July 1, 1995) and the NRHP number. The record's 1933 build year is kept as NHLR's figure; Willhite and firelookout.com say 1932 at Lion Rock, which is noted in the story and the resolved conflicts. Staffing (every summer) comes from undated NHLR, firelookout.com and Willhite pages; no 2025-2026 staffing source was read. A Wenatchee World search snippet says the lookout is staffed annually, but that article returned HTTP 429 and was not read. The 2025 Lower Sugarloaf fire threat is from firelookout.com only. The NRHP entry was read as the NPGallery summary page; the full nomination was not read. Access is public: a gated spur road with a short walk, per WTA and Willhite. No climbing advice is given.
